section_summary: This section traces U.S. deliberations over rebuilding Japan’s merchant marine, including coastwise freight, shipbuilding limits, access to foreign ports, and opposition from American shipowners. It also contains reports of violence, theft, and mistreatment affecting Japanese crews in Korean ports. A lengthy Army study argues for expanding Japanese shipping and coordinating a State–Army policy.

subfiles.title: Conversation on Japanese shipbuilding and shipping
subfiles.about: Officials discussed priorities for Japanese shipping and likely U.S. reactions.
subfiles.summary: The group favored coastwise bulk transport and cautioned against emphasizing overseas tonnage or U.S. ship charters.

subfiles.title: Japanese Merchant Marine
subfiles.about: The consulate forwarded a Chinese shipping federation’s appeal opposing expansion of Japanese shipping.
subfiles.summary: The enclosed letter sought limits on Japanese tonnage and indemnity for Chinese merchant ship losses.

subfiles.title: Enclosure identification for despatch no. 593
subfiles.from: Office of the Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The sheet identifies an enclosure on private owners’ responsibility for Japanese vessels.
subfiles.summary: Identifies enclosure four to a September 1948 despatch.

subfiles.title: Japanese Merchant Marine
subfiles.from: G. P. Lynch, Civil Affairs Division
subfiles.to: Office of the Assistant Secretary of State for Occupied Areas
subfiles.about: The Army transmitted SCAP’s comments on an American shipping federation letter.
subfiles.summary: Forwards SCAP comments and copies of the Bailey correspondence.

subfiles.title: Request for commentary on Bailey statement
subfiles.from: H. B. Lewis, Acting Adjutant General
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: The Army requested a critique of Frazer Bailey’s statement on Japanese merchant shipping.
subfiles.summary: Requests an airmail critique and encloses Bailey’s September 22 statement.

subfiles.title: SCAP reply on Japanese merchant marine
subfiles.to: The Adjutant General, Department of the Army
subfiles.about: SCAP responded to Bailey’s assumptions about fleet size and overseas trade.
subfiles.summary: SCAP says neither a four-million-ton fleet nor final trading areas had been decided.

subfiles.title: Brief and commentary on National Federation of American Shipping letter
subfiles.about: SCAP evaluated American shipowners’ objections to rebuilding Japan’s merchant marine.
subfiles.summary: Paragraph-by-paragraph comments reject fixed tonnage limits and emphasize shipping’s foreign-exchange value. SCAP argues that curbs would chiefly benefit other maritime nations and supports phased rehabilitation, including limited far-seas trade.

subfiles.title: Imbalance between movement of freight intra-Japan by rail and water
subfiles.from: Acting U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch examined why bulk freight remained on overburdened railways.
subfiles.summary: Depressed rail rates and water-terminal charges discouraged coastal shipping. It considered rate changes or a rail embargo on specified bulk cargoes, with more coastwise tonnage.

subfiles.title: Extracts from GHQ FEC press release on freight rates
subfiles.about: Edward Juliber described distorted Japanese rail and water freight rates.
subfiles.summary: Reports rising rail traffic and losses caused by freight rates below operating costs.

subfiles.title: Policy aspects of entry of Japanese merchant ships into U.S. ports
subfiles.about: Moseley urgently requested views on policy barriers to Japanese ships entering U.S. ports.
subfiles.summary: The Army sought a reply before Secretary Royall’s Japan visit.

subfiles.title: Legal aspects of ex-enemy merchant ships calling at U.S. ports
subfiles.about: The Army asked State to identify any policy barring Japanese ships from U.S. ports.
subfiles.summary: Army found no apparent bar and requested a reply by January 26.

subfiles.title: Duplicate Army memorandum on ex-enemy ships
subfiles.about: A second copy repeats the Army’s request about Japanese entry into U.S. ports.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of the preceding memorandum.

subfiles.title: Policy aspects regarding entry of Japanese merchant ships into U.S. ports
subfiles.to: Executive Officer, Civil Affairs Division, Department of the Army
subfiles.about: State proposed delaying final approval of port entry pending wider consultation.
subfiles.summary: The draft supports eventual entry but recommends government, congressional, labor, and industry consultation first.

subfiles.title: Protection of Japanese seamen in Korean ports
subfiles.about: The despatch forwarded a diplomatic note and reports concerning Japanese crews in Korea.
subfiles.summary: Transmits the February 4 note and supporting correspondence.

subfiles.title: Diplomatic note to Korean Liaison Mission
subfiles.about: SCAP sought protection and orderly reception for Japanese ships and crews in Korean ports.
subfiles.summary: Reports mistreatment and asks the Korean government to take protective steps.

subfiles.title: Protection of Japanese seamen in South Korean ports
subfiles.about: The memorandum assembled complaints and earlier safeguards for Japanese crews in Korean ports.
subfiles.summary: It urges assurances from South Korea and enforcement of protective procedures at Pusan and other ports.

subfiles.title: Protection of Japanese seamen in the port of Pusan
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: The Navy warned that withdrawal of U.S. guards could expose Japanese crews to violence.
subfiles.summary: Citing repeated intimidation and theft, it urged effective protection or alternative transport for cargo bound for Pusan.

subfiles.title: Conditions at Pusan
subfiles.from: General Maritime Bureau, Ministry of Transportation
subfiles.to: Naval Shipping Control Authority for Japanese Merchant Marine
subfiles.about: A shipmaster reported deteriorating protection and abuse by Korean port officials.
subfiles.summary: The report describes removal of guards, uncontrolled boarding, coercive quarantine demands, and assault by a customs officer.

subfiles.title: Misconduct of Koreans at the port of Pusan
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: The Navy forwarded a report of misconduct at Pusan.
subfiles.summary: Requests appropriate action on the enclosed report.

subfiles.title: Conditions at Pusan
subfiles.to: Naval Shipping Control Authority for Japanese Merchant Marine
subfiles.about: Japanese shipmasters described theft, intimidation, and inadequate security at Pusan.
subfiles.summary: The report recounts two ships’ experiences with intrusive guards, suspected theft, and attempted pilferage. It asks for more reliable protection aboard Japanese vessels.

subfiles.title: Protection of Japanese seamen in the port of Pusan
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: The Navy forwarded a further report on conditions at Pusan.
subfiles.summary: Submits another Japanese account for information and action.

subfiles.title: Conditions at Pusan
subfiles.to: Naval Shipping Control Authority for Japanese Merchant Marine
subfiles.about: A shipmaster reported Korean officials’ attempts to force stowaways onto a Japan-bound vessel.
subfiles.summary: The master refused the demands, appealed to U.S. authorities, and departed without port assistance.

subfiles.title: Protective measures for Japanese ships at Pusan
subfiles.about: The message described guards, patrols, and incident reporting for Japanese vessels.
subfiles.summary: Lists harbor security measures and reporting requirements at Pusan and other Korean ports.

subfiles.title: Attacks and robberies against personnel on SCAP vessels
subfiles.from: South Korean Interim Government, Bureau of Marine Transportation
subfiles.about: The bureau directed protection for Japanese crews and vessels after attacks and thefts.
subfiles.summary: Requests coast guard and police assistance.

subfiles.title: Violence and pilferage on Japanese-manned vessels in Korean ports
subfiles.from: South Korean Interim Government, Bureau of Marine Transportation
subfiles.about: The bureau required shipmasters to report violence, pilferage, or satisfactory treatment.
subfiles.summary: Directs continuous guards and prompt reporting of incidents.

subfiles.title: Report form for Japanese-manned vessels
subfiles.from: South Korean Interim Government, Bureau of Marine Transportation
subfiles.about: The form records mistreatment or certifies satisfactory treatment in port.
subfiles.summary: Blank form for reports required by bureau instructions.

subfiles.title: Requirement that Allied representatives accompany Japanese-owned vessels
subfiles.about: State proposed conditions for removing Allied representatives from Japanese vessels.
subfiles.summary: The draft requires prior consent from destination governments and continued SCAP control.

subfiles.title: Requirement that Allied representatives accompany Japanese-owned vessels
subfiles.about: Moseley answered a Navy inquiry on representatives aboard vessels bound for the Persian Gulf.
subfiles.summary: Encloses State’s memorandum to the Army on the issue.

subfiles.title: Restrictions on Japanese shipbuilding and shipping
subfiles.about: The memorandum reviewed FEC policies and proposals affecting Japanese shipping capacity.
subfiles.summary: It finds no effective legal restriction on SCAP’s current authority but says FEC intentions and other countries’ views warrant consideration. It summarizes proposed limits on shipbuilding, fleet size, and reparations.

subfiles.title: Forwarding memorandum on shipping restrictions
subfiles.about: Saltzman forwarded the restrictions analysis for comparison with German policy.
subfiles.summary: Suggests sharing the analysis with Murphy and Radius.

subfiles.title: Implementation of NSC 13/2 on merchant shipping
subfiles.about: Radius requested updates on implementing Japanese shipping provisions in NSC 13/2.
subfiles.summary: He cites Maritime Commission and Navy interest and assigns Nickell to follow the issue.

subfiles.title: Proposal for a State–Army shipping policy group
subfiles.about: The Army proposed a joint group to develop policy on Japanese shipping and shipbuilding.
subfiles.summary: Forwards an initial study and seeks an agreed draft for possible NSC submission.

subfiles.title: Japanese Merchant Marine
subfiles.about: The study argued for rebuilding Japan’s merchant marine and opening foreign ports to its vessels.
subfiles.summary: The study links Japanese shipping to foreign exchange, domestic freight, employment, and economic self-support. It reviews occupation policies, reparations proposals, ship construction, charter restrictions, and U.S. port access. Its recommendations include more construction, pursuit of foreign port rights, and a joint State–Army policy for National Security Council consideration.

subfiles.title: Japanese Merchant Marine
subfiles.about: American steamship owners began presenting their views on postwar Japanese shipping policy.
subfiles.summary: The opening page states their concern for U.S. shipping and asks where policy decisions will be made.
